Critical source fidelity: retain the deliberately almost-black face and hair silhouette. The yellow mascot material is seen only as the very faint dark yellow-brown outline permitted by the original light. Match the extremely low exposure of the original, not a normal well-lit character. Preserve its screen-left face direction, dark swept/side-combed hair contour and subtle mouth/eye visibility. Do not infer a beard or other hair from black shadows. No new cap, glasses or decorations.
Keep the head and neck virtually as dark as the original. No golden wedge on the screen-right cheek or neck, no bright rim around the hair, no added side key light, no illuminated yellow neck, and no bright eye glow. Do not lift the black facial shadows to display mascot detail. The source has only a very faint dark warm lower contour, not a bright side of the face. Preserve source light direction and intensity.
Transform visible anatomy into the smooth compact round golden-yellow mascot with the original pose, crop and hair, while respecting that the actual dark lighting hides most facial detail. Keep the original dark civilian suit and lapels, dim pale-gray shirt and dark tie. Seat the short broad curved head base low in a properly fitted source collar; no long yellow stalk, narrow ring, floating collar or cream neck bib.
Preserve exactly one tilted plain gray photograph frame, the fully opaque smoky gray-blue photographic backing, and one overlapping cream paper note on the right. Keep exactly the original two compact upper rows of indistinct dark note-mark groups in the same footprint; no third row, extra writing or invented readable text. Retain the complete source framing and asset aspect ratio. No new ornamental frame engraving, comparison board, caption or watermark.
Keep all original solid surfaces, dark clothes and internal photograph backing opaque. Genuine alpha exists only outside the complete original card silhouette and its real soft edge. Darkness is opaque near-black pigment, never transparent holes. Preserve output full resolution and painterly detail without inventing visible lighting. This source is intentionally a nearly black silhouette; retain that appearance.
Output alpha: genuine transparent RGBA ONLY OUTSIDE the complete original photograph FRAME AND NOTE silhouette. The photographic BACKING INSIDE the frame is a required OPAQUE surface: preserve its original background color and texture behind the character all the way to the inner frame rim. Never turn the gaps between frame and character into transparent holes or a window. Keep the actual tilted photo rectangle, frame rim and overlapping note intact. Do not invent a new backdrop outside the whole card. Retain source clothing, hair, headgear, lighting and crop at full generated resolution. All originally OPAQUE subject surfaces must remain FULLY OPAQUE (alpha 255): yellow head/body, hair, beard, dark or black clothing, coat lapels, collar, tie, buttons and decorations. Dark cloth is colored material, not transparent background. Never fade garment interiors into semi-transparent patches, holes, white haze or see-through fabric. Keep any genuine source outer-edge alpha falloff only at that actual exterior boundary; preserve actual source transparency rather than making the subject itself translucent.
